ledger.claim: The fare breakdown bills SGD 3.00 for the 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City)' gantry, but the driver's own trace never crosses it: the nearest fix to that gantry (index 114, 13:25:40) is 2,608.77 m away, more than ten times the 250 m match radius, and the fare record's own fields say on_optimal_route = false and crossed = false. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure refunded in full, and that correction is available whether or not any deviation exists.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd 43.10, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however the trip is characterised; POL-RD-11(a) governs instead. Charged_total is 46.10. The only pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 are ERP gantries actually crossed (0.00 - the sole AYE line was not crossed), a properly chargeable airport surcharge (0.00 - this trip neither originates nor ends at Changi or Seletar), and the waiting-time fee (0.00). 46.10 less (43.10 plus 0.00) is 3.00, which POL-RD-11(a) refunds in full.

The driver's answer - that the rider accepted the route change in the app and 'the fare is whatever the app calculated' - does not make the toll chargeable. Under POL-RD-09 and POL-RD-11(a) a pass-through line is properly chargeable only where the gantry is actually crossed, and the rider's acceptance of a route says nothing about a gantry on that route that the vehicle never reached. Charging the rider for an ERP line the car never drove under is exactly the billing-integrity defect POL-RD-09(4) exists to correct, and the driver's own statement ('I used local roads') confirms he did not take the expressway the rider accepted.

The driver cannot get the change treated as a rider-caused detour that would bar the ERP refund under POL-RD-09(3). All five chat messages run one way: four driver demands to accept the change ('too many traffic lights this way, can accept the new route?', 'press accept pls, faster for you', 'accept the route change', '??') and the rider's resigned 'ok fine'. No rider message names a road or place, and every message carries waypoint_hint = null. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction naming a place or road, corroborated by waypoint_hint or the trace; with waypoint_hint null and no road named the corroboration test is undecidable, the clause is unavailable, and no rider-caused detour can be found.

The driver's uncited traffic explanation carries no weight. His statement that 'traffic on the expressway then got bad' asserts an external traffic cause, which under POL-RD-13 is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00516-01, is MISSING - status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and POL-RD-03 is unavailable. The driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, so POL-RD-13(1) applies: an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and this is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction. Under POL-RD-08 an uncited assertion is discarded and cannot supply an amended optimal or reduce the excess.

Measured on the fields POL-RD-01 makes governing, the trace records no deviation: excess_km 0.6 (5.36%) fails both the 0.8 km absolute threshold and the 20% threshold, and re-testing against the amended optimal of 11.6 km recorded after the 13:10:40 dropoff amendment under POL-RD-05 reduces the excess to 0.2 km. The rider does not seek a recomputation of the fare on the distance lines - under POL-RD-11 the upfront quote fixed them. The live and only contested charge is the 3.00 pass-through line identified above, and that is what the rider asks be returned.

The only charge line without a counterpart in the trace is the AYE gantry, and it is refunded under POL-RD-09(4); POL-RD-09(4) states in terms that POL-RD-10(8) is not thereby triggered where the only unmatched line is one refunded under that limb. POL-GEN-03 confirms the billing-integrity finding is a REFERRAL that is recorded alongside the money and does not suppress or replace it. The case therefore does not escalate on this ground and a monetary ruling should issue.

The rider's route-deviation claim fails on its own evidence. The governing measurement is the trace, and gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.8 km against a booked optimal of 11.2 km: an excess of 0.6 km, or 5.36% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH gates to pass - more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal - and neither does, so no deviation is established and the outcome on the deviation is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

Even measured the way most favourable to the rider - against the amended optimal of 11.6 km stored on the trip record after the in-app route change that produced this dispute - the excess is 0.2 km, roughly 1.7% of optimal, which again fails both POL-RD-01 gates. POL-RD-05 requires the comparison to be re-run against the amended endpoints, and on that recomputation no deviation survives either.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 43.10. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The rider's demand for the charged total of 46.10 is unavailable on those components as a matter of policy, not discretion.

POL-RD-08 puts the initial burden on the rider to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare ledger, but the threshold excess is simply absent from an unimpaired trace, so the rider's burden is never discharged and the driver is not put to any exculpatory clause at all.

The route change was rider-accepted on the record: the rider's own message 'ok fine' is sent at 13:10:35 and the dropoff amendment is recorded at 13:10:40 on the trip record, so the amended itinerary is a route change of the kind POL-RD-05 addresses. Under POL-RD-09(3), where the route change is rider-caused under POL-RD-05, no ERP refund is due.

The contested sum of 46.10 cannot stand in any event. No distance-or-time component is refundable on this upfront-quoted trip under POL-RD-11 and no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, which leaves at most the single 3.00 ERP line. I do not overstate the driver's position on that line: the trace's closest approach to the AYE gantry is 2608.77 m, well outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) uses, so if the tribunal treats the line as unmatched the only correction this record supports is 3.00, and nothing the rider has claimed on top of it.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 169 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is not met, no independent corroboration is required and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation trigger does not fire. The driver's remark that expressway traffic turned bad names no advisory evidence ID, so under POL-RD-13(1) the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact and does not force escalation under POL-RD-10(5). For the avoidance of doubt I disclose that the advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00516-01 carries status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact; its absence is citable and is citable only as absence. The case should be decided on the money, not held.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and driver: The distance-and-time part of this dispute is not refundable. This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (quoted_fare_sgd 43.10), so POL-RD-11 fixes distance and time at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run. On the route-deviation test, the GPS trace is 11.8 km against a booked optimal of 11.2 km, an excess of 0.6 km (5.36%), and even against the amended optimal of 11.6 km the excess is 0.2 km. Both fail the POL-RD-01 gates of more than 0.8 km and more than 20%, so no deviation is established. The trace is not impaired for POL-RD-07 purposes: 169 fixes at 10-second cadence, 100% coverage and no gaps. The driver's uncited traffic explanation is not weighed: it names no advisory evidence ID, and the only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00516-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, so under POL-RD-13 it does not force escalation under POL-RD-10(5). The driver's argument that the rider accepted the route change does not bar the ERP correction either: the rider's 'ok fine' accepted a route change, but the driver's own statement says he used local roads, so the AYE gantry was never crossed. The refund is the single 3.00 ERP line. The fare contains a 3.00 charge for the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City) gantry, but the trace's closest fix to it is 2,608.77 m away, far outside the 250 m match radius, and the fare record itself says on_optimal_route false and crossed false. Under POL-RD-09(4) that is a billing-integrity failure and the 3.00 is refunded in full. POL-RD-11(a) gives the same result: charged_total 46.10 less quoted_fare 43.10 less properly chargeable pass-throughs 0.00 equals 3.00. I have not added a second POL-RD-11(b) correction for the same line. No repeat-deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 250. There is no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral and no driver compensation, since billed distance matches the trace and no POL-RD-04 shortfall is shown. Confidence is 0.95, capped at 1.0 by the GPS trace and fare breakdown that carry the deciding fact.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity review: refund the SGD 3.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City) ERP line charged for a gantry the GPS trace never crossed (nearest fix 2,608.77 m, outside the 250 m match radius); record the billing-integrity finding.
